title: A Structural Voyage Across the Size Spectrum: Architecture of Salmonella Phages from Microviridae to Jumbo
content: Salmonella enterica (S. enterica) is a leading cause of foodborne illness worldwide, and the accelerating spread of multidrug-resistant serovars has renewed interest in bacteriophages as therapeutic agents. Phages infecting S. enterica exhibit an extraordinary diversity of virion architectures, ranging from compact, non-tailed microviruses with circular, single-stranded DNA genomes to jumbo phages with large, double-stranded DNA genomes and elaborately layered capsid–tail assemblies. Here, we review this architecture by morphotype: microviruses (Microviridae), podoviruses, siphoviruses, myoviruses and jumbo phages. Each section centers on representative, structurally characterized phages as focal case studies. By integrating available cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) reconstructions with complementary biochemical and genomic evidence, we distinguish features conserved within a morphotype from those reflecting lineage-specific adaptation. For each morphotype, we further discuss how these architectures address key functional imperatives, including protection of the genome in the extracellular environment and recognition of diverse Salmonella surface receptors. By linking virion architecture to function, this review identifies key gaps for future mechanistic studies and informs the rational selection and engineering of phages against multidrug-resistant Salmonella.
